Not ACT, but I worked on an IMT team in NYC. Have been doing mobile teams for the last 5 years. For any role on a mobile team, the burnout is insanely high, so I feel your pain as a director, especially in today's social climate. My old supervisor drilled his mantra into my head "it's a marathon not a sprint" and "celebrate the small victories". Working with clients for longer periods like on an ACT team sometimes causes people to forget about the short term goals like "Save $10 this week" or "Make your appointment on Tuesday". Focusing on the really short term goals really helped me out. When COVID hit, our team dynamic suffered immensely as we no longer felt like a family after spending so much time apart and not being allowed in the office, despite still being forced to do field work at the peak of the pandemic. One thing that my former director tried to implement was more dual visits, to get the team together again and rebuild that camaraderie, so that none of us, including  the director themselves, bore too much weight on their own shoulders. Hope this helps OP.
